newsitem.title: GERMANY: Munich Re says to raise 95/96 dividend to 16 dmk.
newsitem.headline: Munich Re says to raise 95/96 dividend to 16 dmk.

text.p: The world's biggest reinsurer, Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG, or Munich Re, on Thursday said it would raise its dividend for the 1996/1996 business year to 16 marks ($10.51) from 13 marks.
The Munich-based giant said in a statement its profit situation had been "extraordinary" in the business year which ended June 30 and that its earnings per share had more than doubled to 140 marks.
The group said the main push for its profit rise was a continued improvement in its underwriting earnings, but did not give further details. These will be given at a news conference on November 11.

Munich Re, whose registered shares took their long-awaited place on Germany's blue chip DAX index last September after a long campaign, also said it planned to reduce the nominal value of its shares to help make them more liquid.
Its registered shares jumped 114 marks to 3,570 marks on the news in post-bourse dealings.
The group plans to propose a 10-for-one stock split to reduce the par value of registered shares to 10 marks each and the par value of bearer shares to five marks.
The move, in line with similar actions by several leading German companies, would reduce the price of Munich Re stock to around one tenth of their current level.
Munich Re said the move was "a further step in investors' interests" following the DAX inclusion.
